paragraphs: Value iteration repeatedly applies a Bellman operator to improve value estimates in reinforcement learning. Its familiar convergence rate depends on the discount factor, gamma. When gamma is close to one, the standard guarantee can become weak. This paper asks whether value iteration can be accelerated in a general way and how fast such an accelerated method could possibly be.

The proposed algorithm, Anc-VI, introduces an anchoring mechanism distinct from Nesterov acceleration. It applies to both Bellman consistency and optimality operators and reduces Bellman error faster than standard value iteration. In the regime where gamma is approximately one, including gamma equal to one, the authors establish an O(1/k) rate. They contrast this with an O(1) rate for standard value iteration when gamma is at least 1 − 1/k.

A complexity lower bound matches the accelerated upper bound within a factor of four, establishing the rate's optimality in the studied setup. The authors also extend the acceleration benefit to approximate value iteration and Gauss–Seidel value iteration, showing that anchoring reaches beyond the basic update scheme.
neurips-2023-accelerating-value-iteratio.tldr: Anc-VI uses anchoring to accelerate Bellman-error reduction, with an optimal rate up to a constant factor in the studied setting.

paragraphs: Models trained on tables often encounter deployment data that differ from their training data. Despite the widespread use of tabular prediction, its robustness under such changes has been less well characterized than robustness for images and text. TableShift supplies a common benchmark for studying this problem across 15 binary classification tasks, each paired with a distribution shift.

The tasks span finance, education, public policy, healthcare, and civic participation. The authors compare leading tabular models with robust learning and domain generalization methods. Across this study, accuracy on familiar data and accuracy on shifted data follow a linear trend. Methods designed for domain robustness can narrow the performance gap, but the observed improvement comes with reduced accuracy on familiar data.

The study also finds a strong relationship between performance gaps and changes in the label distribution. These findings make a smaller shift gap something to interpret alongside both underlying accuracies. The released benchmark and Python interface provide a shared basis for examining these tradeoffs across different prediction problems.
neurips-2023-benchmarking-distribution-s.tldr: TableShift benchmarks 15 tabular classification tasks and reveals empirical relationships among distribution shifts, accuracy gaps, and robustness tradeoffs.

paragraphs: Automatic dialogue evaluators score how coherently a response fits a conversation. Self-supervised training has produced strong evaluators, but the training examples can have an uneven distribution of coherence levels. The paper connects this imbalance to poor agreement with people on moderately coherent responses. Its theoretical analysis also identifies a danger that uneven output score distributions can weaken robustness.

The proposed BCR framework addresses the training examples and the resulting scores together. It reconstructs the training set to provide more balanced signals across coherence levels. It also introduces a loss that adapts to the estimated uniformity of the score distribution, using kernel density estimation to measure that distribution. These components aim to improve evaluation across the coherence range.

Across 17 benchmark datasets, a BERT-base evaluator trained with BCR reportedly exceeds state-of-the-art methods by 11.3% on average. Applying BCR to several existing leading methods also improves correlation and robustness. The findings support balancing the learning signals and output scores as a useful intervention for the evaluated dialogue models.
neurips-2023-better-correlation-and-robu.tldr: BCR balances coherence examples and evaluator scores to improve agreement with human dialogue judgments and robustness.

paragraphs: Differentially private linear regression often asks users to supply precise data bounds or algorithm settings. Choosing those settings can require inspecting the sensitive data, undermining the intended privacy protection. Algorithms that make more of these decisions automatically reduce that burden, but their predictive usefulness can deteriorate as the number of input features grows.

This paper adds a private feature-selection stage before regression. The selection method uses Kendall rank correlation to identify useful features while maintaining differential privacy. Reducing the feature set addresses the dimensionality problem before the regression algorithm runs. The authors prove a utility guarantee for the setting in which the features are normally distributed; that assumption is part of the stated theoretical result.

Experiments across 25 datasets show that this preliminary selection step substantially expands the applicability of existing plug-and-play private regression algorithms. The reported gains require little additional privacy expenditure, computation, or user decision-making. The contribution therefore concerns both prediction and usability: private regression becomes useful across a broader range of feature dimensions without returning the tuning burden to users.
neurips-2023-better-private-linear-regre.tldr: Private feature selection based on Kendall rank correlation makes plug-and-play private linear regression useful in higher-dimensional problems.

paragraphs: Web images provide abundant training data, but their labels and accompanying text can be misleading. Ambiguous queries may retrieve images dominated by the wrong concept, making fine-grained categories especially difficult to learn. CAPro addresses this problem by using images and text together to build class representatives, or prototypes, whose meaning matches the intended category.

Textual prototypes come from class definitions and help identify clean images through text matching. Those images guide the visual prototypes. Because accompanying text may be missing or mismatched, visual features also help complete and improve the text information. High-quality samples further refine the visual prototypes, which support clustering and noise removal. A collective bootstrapping mechanism draws label guidance from visually similar examples.

Experiments on WebVision1k and NUS-WIDE (Web) report state-of-the-art performance under realistic noise in both single-label and multi-label settings, alongside robustness in open-set recognition. The central finding is that aligning category meaning across text and images helps the evaluated models learn useful visual concepts even when web supervision is unreliable.
neurips-2023-capro-webly-supervised-lear.tldr: CAPro aligns text and image prototypes to learn visual categories from web data with noisy labels and unreliable accompanying text.

paragraphs: Distributed optimization often requires a server to average vectors held by multiple clients. Sending every coordinate is expensive, so Rand-k sparsification transmits only k coordinates from each d-dimensional vector. This saves communication but ignores relationships between clients. An existing correlation-aware estimator, Rand-k-Spatial, uses those relationships at the server, yet the paper identifies room to improve its estimation performance.

The proposed Rand-Proj-Spatial method changes what clients transmit. It projects each vector into a random k-dimensional subspace, generalizing the coordinate-selection approach. Using a Subsampled Randomized Hadamard Transform for this projection, the authors show improved performance over Rand-k-Spatial through more effective use of cross-client correlation information.

The paper also develops a way to handle different degrees of correlation and proposes a practical variant for servers without that information. Experiments on real-world distributed optimization tasks report improvements over Rand-k-Spatial and other sparsification methods. The contribution connects communication compression with the shared structure of client vectors, targeting better mean estimates within distributed learning.
neurips-2023-correlation-aware-sparsifie.tldr: Rand-Proj-Spatial combines random projections with cross-client correlation information to improve communication-efficient distributed mean estimation.

paragraphs: Transformer design often emphasizes prediction accuracy and computational cost, while corrupted or adversarial samples receive less attention. This paper approaches robustness by reinterpreting self-attention as a nonparametric kernel density estimator. That connection lets the authors adapt established robust estimation techniques to the computation that determines how information is combined inside a transformer.

The first family of methods reduces the influence of outliers in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space when computing attention. Empirical results show improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods, particularly for image data exposed to adversarial attacks. The approach matters because it places resistance to unusual samples within the attention operation itself.

A second approach uses the median-of-means principle to obtain an efficient robust attention method. The authors report improved performance and robustness on language modeling and time series classification. These methods can be combined with existing transformers, making them potential additions to established architectures. The evidence covers several task types, with the reported benefits tied to the experiments described rather than a universal immunity to attacks.
neurips-2023-designing-robust-transforme.tldr: Recasting attention as kernel density estimation yields transformer modifications with improved empirical resistance to attacks and contaminated data.

paragraphs: Diffusion maps reduce dimensionality by using a kernel to describe nonlinear relationships among data points. The paper addresses a restriction of the existing framework: its reliance on symmetric kernels. Directional relationships in graphs and trophic networks do not naturally fit that requirement, because proximity in one direction need not match proximity in the reverse direction.

The authors develop MagDM around a magnetic transform, which converts an asymmetric matrix into a Hermitian matrix. Simply performing that conversion leaves important mathematical questions unresolved. A diffusion representation must retain a meaningful diffusion distance and avoid divergence as diffusion proceeds. The paper supplies a theoretical foundation for a framework using the transform to address these issues.

Experiments on three synthetic datasets and two trophic networks demonstrate effectiveness and robustness for data with asymmetric proximity. The contribution extends the diffusion representation framework to accommodate directional structure. This matters for settings where asymmetry carries information that a method restricted to symmetric relationships cannot directly represent.
neurips-2023-diffusion-representation-fo.tldr: MagDM uses a theoretically grounded magnetic transform to extend diffusion representations to asymmetric relationships.

paragraphs: Human preference comparisons help steer language models toward desired behavior. A common approach first learns a reward model from those comparisons, then uses reinforcement learning to improve the language model while limiting its departure from the original model. This creates a complex training procedure whose separate stages can be difficult to manage.

Direct Preference Optimization uses a mapping between reward functions and optimal policies to reformulate that constrained reward-maximization problem. The resulting training objective works directly with preference comparisons and resembles a classification problem. It removes the need to fit a separate reward model or sample language-model outputs during fine-tuning, and the authors describe it as stable and computationally lightweight.

The experiments find that DPO matches or exceeds existing methods in aligning models with human preferences. Reported results include stronger sentiment control than RLHF and better response quality for summarization and single-turn dialogue. The significance is a simpler route to the stated preference-learning objective, with empirical evidence that this simplification can retain or improve alignment performance.
neurips-2023-direct-preference-optimizat.tldr: DPO trains language models directly on preference comparisons, simplifying preference alignment while matching or improving tested alternatives.

paragraphs: Regression uncertainty should be useful for individual predictions, not only accurate when averaged across a population. This paper studies calibration of predictive quantiles at that individual level. Through examples, it shows that population-level properties such as average calibration or sharpness can coexist with harmful or unexpected outcomes for downstream decisions.

The authors propose nonparametric calibration methods that can be used independently of the underlying prediction model. They establish computational efficiency, statistical consistency, and matching upper and lower bounds on calibration error. Their analysis combines nonparametric techniques with a covering-number argument, connecting individual calibration to the difficulty of estimating distributions as dimension grows.

This perspective helps reconcile earlier impossibility results with attainable calibration guarantees. The paper also presents finite-sample guarantees under minimal assumptions in the conformal prediction context, while explicitly examining the curse of dimensionality. Numerical experiments report advantages across several metrics and under covariate shift. Together, the theory and experiments provide a grounded alternative to largely heuristic approaches to individual regression calibration.
neurips-2023-distribution-free-model-agn.tldr: Nonparametric methods provide model-agnostic individual regression calibration with statistical guarantees that expose the role of dimensionality.

paragraphs: An agent exploring without external rewards or knowledge of its environment needs guidance about what to pursue next. D2C supplies that guidance from a few examples of desired outcomes. It builds a curriculum of intermediate goals without requiring a particular environment geometry or a particular arrangement of the outcome examples.

The method trains diverse goal-conditioned classifiers to compare visited states with desired outcomes. Their disagreement on out-of-distribution states provides a signal about unexplored regions. That signal supports an intrinsic reward conditioned on a goal, giving the agent a way to value exploration relative to the outcomes it seeks.

D2C then uses bipartite matching to define a curriculum objective that produces a sequence of adjusted intermediate goals. This connects identifying unfamiliar regions with choosing actionable exploration targets. Experiments report quantitative and qualitative improvements over earlier curriculum reinforcement learning methods, including when desired examples are arbitrarily distributed. The results support disagreement as a useful source of exploration guidance in the evaluated outcome-directed learning problems.
neurips-2023-diversify-conquer-outcome-d.tldr: D2C turns classifier disagreement and a few desired-outcome examples into intermediate goals for reinforcement learning exploration.

paragraphs: Radar is attractive for autonomous driving because of its cost and performance in bad weather. Its conventional point clouds, however, can be sparse and inaccurate because angular resolution is limited. The processing that creates those point clouds also removes weak signals to reduce false targets, potentially discarding information useful to a learned sensor-fusion model.

EchoFusion bypasses the existing radar processing pipeline to incorporate raw radar information with other sensors. It first creates bird's-eye-view queries, then retrieves corresponding radar spectrum features for fusion. This gives the model access to distance and speed information from radar echoes together with semantic information from images.

On the RADIal dataset, the authors report performance above existing methods and approaching that of LiDAR. These results support retaining richer radar measurements for the evaluated fusion task. The broader design contribution is to reconsider where sensor information enters a learning system: processing decisions intended to clean up individual sensor outputs can remove signals that are useful when multiple sensors are interpreted together.
neurips-2023-echoes-beyond-points-unleas.tldr: EchoFusion combines radar spectrum features with other sensors, improving detection on RADIal by retaining information lost during point-cloud generation.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can generate stochastic processes, extending generation from finite collections of values to functions. Scientific problems often add geometric requirements: outputs may inhabit non-Euclidean spaces, and transformations should preserve meaningful symmetries. This paper extends diffusion modeling in infinite-dimensional settings to incorporate those requirements directly.

The construction has two coordinated parts. The noising process approaches a geometric Gaussian process that transforms according to the relevant symmetry group. The neural network approximating the score is equivariant under that same group, so its outputs transform consistently with its inputs. The authors show that these conditions give the resulting generative functional model the corresponding symmetry.

A new conditional sampler based on Langevin methods supports demonstrations on complex scalar and vector fields, including fields with Euclidean and spherical output spaces. Experiments use synthetic data and real-world weather data to demonstrate capacity and scalability. The contribution links a mathematical symmetry guarantee to a generative modeling framework for geometrically structured scientific quantities.
neurips-2023-geometric-neural-diffusion-.tldr: Geometric neural diffusion processes combine symmetry-aware noise and equivariant score networks to generate functions with matching geometric symmetries.

paragraphs: Maintaining a large engineering system requires coordinating decisions across components whose damage can threaten the whole system. IMP-MARL represents this challenge as cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning. Each agent schedules inspections and repairs for one component, working to reduce maintenance expense while cooperating to control system failure risk.

The open-source suite provides several infrastructure-management environments, including one concerned with offshore wind structures. Environments with up to 100 agents allow researchers to test how learning methods behave as coordination grows more demanding. The benchmark compares leading cooperative reinforcement learning approaches with expert-designed heuristic policies.

In the reported experiments, centralized training followed by decentralized execution scales better with agent count than fully centralized or fully decentralized reinforcement learning. It also outperforms expert heuristics in most of the environments. These findings identify a promising training arrangement for the tested management problems while leaving cooperation and scalability challenges to address. The suite provides an engineering-focused platform for studying those challenges and adding further environments.
neurips-2023-imp-marl-a-suite-of-environ.tldr: IMP-MARL benchmarks cooperative infrastructure maintenance with up to 100 agents and finds advantages for centralized training with decentralized execution.

paragraphs: An activity looks very different through the participant's camera and through an outside observer's camera. Linking these views requires representations that retain fine-grained action information despite the visual change. Earlier approaches relied on synchronized video pairs. This paper learns from videos that need not share a recording time or environment.

The AE2 method uses temporal alignment to connect first-person and third-person activity sequences. Its encoder focuses explicitly on hands and the objects being used. A contrastive alignment objective treats temporally reversed frames as negative examples, making action order part of the learning signal. These designs combine attention to the relevant interaction with sensitivity to how it unfolds.

The authors create a four-dataset benchmark for fine-grained understanding across these viewpoints, including a collected first-person tennis forehand dataset and dense frame labels for evaluation. AE2 strongly outperforms prior work across multiple downstream tasks in both regular and cross-view settings. The findings support learning detailed shared action features while relaxing the need for synchronized training recordings.
neurips-2023-learning-fine-grained-view-.tldr: AE2 learns fine-grained action representations across first-person and third-person videos through temporal alignment without synchronized recordings.

paragraphs: Inferring the behavior of interacting experts involves understanding both what they seek and what constrains their actions. This paper studies that problem when demonstrations arrive sequentially and are distributed among several learners. The learners must update their estimates as information arrives while coordinating their understanding through intermittent communication.

The authors formulate the task as distributed online bilevel optimization. The outer problem estimates reward functions, while the inner problem learns constraints and the corresponding policies. Their MA-BIRDS algorithm handles both levels within a single loop. This design joins behavior inference and policy learning in the same ongoing distributed procedure.

The analysis guarantees that learners reach consensus on rewards, constraints, and policies. Over N iterations, average local regret decreases as O(1/N^(1−η1) + 1/N^(1−η2) + 1/N), while cumulative constraint violation grows as O(N^η2 + 1), with both parameters between one-half and one. Thus, the stated constraint bound permits violations to accumulate but at a sublinear rate, alongside diminishing average local regret.
neurips-2023-learning-multi-agent-behavi.tldr: MA-BIRDS infers multi-agent rewards, constraints, and policies from distributed streaming demonstrations with consensus and online performance guarantees.

paragraphs: Scalp EEG offers plentiful unlabeled data for pre-training, but datasets can use different selections of recording channels. Those differences complicate learning a shared representation across resources. At the same time, the channels carry structural and spatial information that could help a model understand the recordings if that information is represented consistently.

The paper proposes mapping different channel selections onto a unified topology. It then builds the MMM pre-training framework on that shared organization. MMM combines multidimensional position encoding, a multilevel channel hierarchy, and a multistage training strategy. Together, these components aim to produce representations that are less tied to a particular channel arrangement while still using EEG geometry.

Experiments on emotion-recognition benchmark datasets report substantial improvements over previous state-of-the-art techniques. The approach therefore provides empirical support for coordinating channel structure before and during pre-training. Its central contribution is a route toward cross-dataset EEG learning in which differing channel selections can share a representation framework, with the demonstrated downstream benefit in emotion recognition.
neurips-2023-learning-topology-agnostic-.tldr: MMM maps different EEG channel selections to a shared topology and uses geometric pre-training to improve emotion recognition.

paragraphs: Detecting ships and floating objects from aerial imagery is difficult when targets are distant and the sea introduces reflections, wind effects, and waves. Hyperspectral sensors offer more than 100 visible and near-infrared channels, which can reveal material information from only a few pixels. The paper investigates this information as a way to reduce confusion caused by the water surface.

The authors collect and annotate M²SODAI, a dataset of synchronized RGB and hyperspectral image pairs. It includes bounding boxes for nearly 6,000 instances per category. Providing paired observations addresses the scarcity of public hyperspectral detection datasets and enables direct study of how these sensor types can complement one another.

The paper also introduces DoubleFPN, a multimodal extension of a feature pyramid network. Experiments on the new benchmark show that combining RGB and hyperspectral data can improve mean average precision, particularly when sea-surface effects are present. The dataset and model together establish a concrete setting for evaluating spectral information in maritime object detection.
neurips-2023-m-2-sodai-multi-modal-marit.tldr: M²SODAI pairs RGB and hyperspectral maritime imagery, and DoubleFPN shows detection gains from fusing the two sensor types.

paragraphs: A policy operating in a changing system must adapt as both costs and dynamics evolve. This paper studies online policy selection in that setting, treating policy adjustment as an online optimization problem. It introduces Gradient-based Adaptive Policy Selection, or GAPS, alongside an analytical framework for understanding its behavior.

The key condition is a proposed notion of contractive policy classes. Under this condition, GAPS approximates an ideal online gradient descent procedure over policy parameters while using less information and computation. That connection provides a way to analyze practical adaptive updates through a better-understood optimization procedure.

The guarantees depend on the problem's structure. When convexity holds, the authors establish optimal policy regret and describe this as the first such result. Without convexity, they provide a local regret bound, which is a different and more local performance statement. Numerical experiments show faster adaptation than existing benchmarks. Together, the results connect a contraction-based theoretical framework with observed responsiveness to environmental change.
neurips-2023-online-adaptive-policy-sele.tldr: GAPS adapts policies in changing systems, with contraction-based regret guarantees and empirical improvements in adaptation speed.

paragraphs: Conventional spiking neurons use a charge, fire, and reset sequence that makes simulation proceed serially through time. The paper connects this structure with difficulty learning long-term dependencies. Its starting observation is that removing the reset permits the neuronal dynamics to be rewritten without an iterative dependence on preceding hidden states.

The resulting Parallel Spiking Neuron, or PSN, allows neuronal dynamics to be computed in parallel. Fully connected input weights make temporal information available across the sequence. For step-by-step inference, a masked version prevents access to future inputs. A further sliding version shares weights across time steps and accommodates sequences of varying lengths.

Evaluations cover simulation speed and classification of temporal and static data. The authors report strong advantages in both efficiency and accuracy for the PSN family. The contribution is a redesign of the neuron's temporal computation, paired with variants for different inference requirements. In particular, the masking mechanism addresses future-input access explicitly when predictions must be made sequentially.
neurips-2023-parallel-spiking-neurons-wi.tldr: Parallel Spiking Neurons remove reset-based recurrence to enable fast parallel computation, with masked and sliding variants for sequential use.

paragraphs: Constrained saddle-point problems combine minimization and maximization and appear in applications such as robust classification and dictionary learning. This paper considers smooth objectives that are nonconvex in the minimizing variables and concave in the maximizing variables. It develops methods that reduce reliance on projections for satisfying constraints.

The first algorithm is a single-loop primal-dual conditional gradient method built using regularization and nested approximation. It handles constraints solely through linear minimization oracles and uses first-order information. If the maximizing constraint set is strongly convex, the method reaches an epsilon-stationary solution within O(epsilon^-6) iterations. Stationarity is the stated target, rather than a guarantee of globally solving the nonconvex problem.

When projection is easy on the maximizing side, a second method uses it there while remaining projection-free on the other side. Its iteration bound is O(epsilon^-4). Strong concavity yields improved complexities for the proposed methods. These results supply convergence guarantees for alternatives whose constraint-handling requirements can better match the structure of a given saddle-point problem.
neurips-2023-projection-free-methods-for.tldr: The paper gives projection-free and partly projection-free saddle-point algorithms with stationarity guarantees under explicit structural assumptions.

paragraphs: Pose models trained on synthetic images need adaptation before working well on real images, but obtaining new pose annotations is costly. Pseudo-labeling can use a model's own predictions as training targets on unlabeled data. Its usefulness is limited when those targets contain errors, including predictions that appear confident despite placing keypoints incorrectly.

This paper complements pseudo-labeling with geometric image reconstruction. Predicted keypoints determine how a base image is transformed to reconstruct a driving image. A reconstruction loss then refines the keypoint predictions. The method provides another training signal for adaptation, allowing image reconstruction to help correct confident but inaccurate locations.

Across four large-scale real-world hand and human datasets, the authors report an 8% improvement in PCK over previous state-of-the-art approaches. They also report gains of 7.2% for fingertips and 29.9% for the head. These results support reconstruction as a useful complement to pseudo-labels when adapting from synthetic training data to an unlabeled real-world target domain.
neurips-2023-synthetic-to-real-pose-esti.tldr: Geometric image reconstruction helps correct pose predictions during synthetic-to-real adaptation using unlabeled target images.

paragraphs: Selective classifiers can decline to answer when uncertain, aiming to avoid confident mistakes. Differential privacy complicates this goal because private training adds randomness. The paper empirically studies how abstention methods behave under privacy constraints, considering both their suitability for privacy protection and their ability to distinguish reliable predictions.

Some popular selective prediction methods are found unsuitable because they increase privacy-leakage risk. A recent method using only checkpoints from an off-the-shelf private training algorithm is particularly suitable. The study also finds that privacy degrades selective classification performance as well as ordinary predictive utility. A proposed evaluation mechanism separates selective prediction behavior across different levels of full-coverage model utility.

The experiments show that private models can recover performance levels attainable by non-private models, but doing so requires a substantial reduction in coverage as the privacy budget decreases. Coverage is the share of cases on which a model answers. The findings therefore expose a practical tradeoff: stronger privacy can require abstaining on considerably more inputs to retain comparable predictive performance.
neurips-2023-training-private-models-tha.tldr: Private selective classifiers can recover non-private performance in experiments, but stronger privacy demands substantially more abstention.

paragraphs: Strong video representations on familiar data may behave differently when the context, viewpoint, actor, or data source changes. This paper systematically studies six self-supervised video methods under these shifts, as well as zero-shot generalization and open-set recognition. It constructs 17 pairs of in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks from public datasets.

The results show that robustness depends on the kind of shift. Video models generally struggle with changes in context, although v-MAE and supervised learning are more robust in that comparison. The study identifies v-MAE as a strong temporal learner, while the contrastive methods v-SimCLR and v-MoCo perform strongly under viewpoint changes.

Another finding concerns recognizing unfamiliar classes: when pretrained encoders are used without fine-tuning, closed-set and open-set recognition performance exhibit a tradeoff. This qualification matters because the observation applies to that encoder-use setting. Overall, the benchmark reveals distinct strengths across learning methods and evaluation conditions, helping characterize what standard video representation performance can leave unresolved about distribution shift.
neurips-2023-uncovering-the-hidden-dynam.tldr: A study of six video self-supervised methods finds shift-specific strengths and a closed-set versus open-set tradeoff without fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Open-vocabulary 3D segmentation aims to identify scene regions using flexible language descriptions, but diverse annotated 3D training data are scarce. Transferring knowledge from 2D segmentation models can help, yet those models may have been fine-tuned on fixed category sets that weaken their open-vocabulary capabilities. This paper instead builds on CLIP and DINO.

Given text descriptions of objects in a scene, the method transfers multimodal knowledge and object reasoning from these foundation models into a neural radiance field. That representation lifts 2D features into 3D segmentation that remains consistent across views. The approach requires no manual segmentation annotations for either the foundation models or the distillation process.

Experiments show that the method exceeds fully supervised segmentation models in certain scenes. The scope of that result matters: the reported advantage is scene-dependent. More broadly, the findings suggest that 2D images and image-text pairs can provide effective supervision for open-vocabulary 3D segmentation, reducing reliance on manually labeled scene regions while preserving a connection to language.
neurips-2023-weakly-supervised-3d-open-v.tldr: Knowledge from CLIP and DINO enables view-consistent open-vocabulary 3D segmentation without manual segmentation annotations.
